summary.intent: Design and implement a full interactive TUI dashboard for the memory-loop CLI subsystem using Charmbracelet/bubbletea libraries, covering all lifecycle management actions in a tab-based interface.
summary.outcome: A complete TUI implementation was scaffolded and built across 9 tasks: package structure (styles, keys, messages, render helpers), root model with cobra command wiring, and all four tabs (Memories, Injection, History, Settings) plus an add-memory form. Final code review issues were partially addressed.

repo: The project uses a `termstyle` package for ANSI 256-color styling that respects NO_COLOR — new TUI should reuse this palette rather than define its own.
Memory lifecycle transitions go through `TransitionRecordLifecycle` in the memoryloop package; the TUI must call this rather than mutating state directly.
The project uses `ACCESSIBLE=1` env var to simplify huh forms — the TUI falls back to plain-text subcommand output in this mode.
Charmbracelet bubbletea TUI code lives in a dedicated package (e.g., `memorylooptui/`) mirroring existing package structure like `memoryloop/`, `insights/`, `settings/`.
go.mod lint failures on uncommitted changes are expected and not real lint errors — the CI check requires committed go.mod changes.

code.finding: Final review fix target — issues around lifecycle action handling, error display, or key conflict resolution were patched here after code review.

workflow: Subagent-driven development works well for sequential but tightly-coupled foundational tasks — Tasks 1-3 were batched into a single implementer dispatch to avoid dependency ordering issues.
The brainstorming visual companion (local HTTP server with HTML mockups) is effective for getting rapid design feedback on TUI layouts before writing specs.
Spec self-review step (placeholder scan, consistency check, scope check, ambiguity check) caught a missing `prune` keybinding before the plan was written.
Code reviewer output should be triaged: some items (async spinner, unit tests) are intentionally deferred per spec scope, while real bugs (key conflicts, error display) need immediate fixes.
Uncommitted changes accumulated across Tasks 5-9 because each subagent implementation didn't auto-commit — a final commit pass is needed after multi-task subagent runs.

friction: Tasks 5-9 produced uncommitted changes that weren't captured in git until a final explicit commit step — subagent implementers didn't consistently commit their work.
go.mod lint error appeared mid-session and required investigation before confirming it was a non-issue (uncommitted go.mod, not a real lint failure).
Code reviewer flagged items (tests, async spinner) that were explicitly out of scope per the spec — reviewer prompt may not have had enough spec context to filter these out.
open_items: Unit tests for the TUI package are deferred — the design spec called for manual verification only; automated tests for bubbletea models should be added later.
Async refresh spinner in the History tab is not yet wired to a real background goroutine — placeholder only.
Code review items 1 (unit tests) and 5 (spinner async wiring) were explicitly deferred and need follow-up.
The `prune` action was added to the keybinding spec during self-review but its full implementation status in the Memories tab should be verified.
Accessible fallback (`ACCESSIBLE=1` → plain-text subcommands) needs to be wired at the cobra command entry point.
